source.check: full names from the Derry Journal's list of nominations (6 May), which says every other nominee was a retiring member except T. H. Goligher; North Ward votes from its result (18 May), M'Farland's figure as fixed by the printed Unionist majority of 352 (the OCR reads 8,392)

note: First May round under the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934: retirement of two councillors and one alderman in each of the five wards of Londonderry Corporation; nominations Tuesday 5 May, poll Friday 15 May 1936. The fifteen retiring members were expected to be returned unopposed, but Patrick Maxwell, a Nationalist South Ward councillor, was nominated at the last minute for the North Ward councillorships as a protest against the proposed revision of the wards; all other seats were filled unopposed (Derry Journal, 6 and 18 May 1936; News-Letter, 6 and 16 May 1936). Poll estimated at 92 per cent (News-Letter). The printed 'Unionist maj. 352' is M'Farland's lead over Maxwell; Finlay's was 11 less, according to the Journal. Plumpers: M'Farland 22, Finlay 17; cross-votes M'Farland-Maxwell 17, Finlay-Maxwell 11.
